questions.question_text: Arrange the words GRAPE, GROWN, GRASS, GROSS and GRIND in dictionary order.
questions.explanation: Compare letter by letter: GRAPE, GRASS, GRIND, GROSS, GROWN. Their labels are 1, 3, 5, 4, 2.
questions.source: Word Building 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: From ORGANISATION, which word cannot be formed using its letters?
questions.explanation: ORANGE requires E, which does not occur in ORGANISATION. The other three words do not exceed any source-letter frequency.
questions.source: Word Building 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: From APPLICATION, which word cannot be formed using its letters?
questions.explanation: POLONIA needs two Os, but APPLICATION contains only one O. POINT, OPTICAL and ANTIC each fit the available letter counts.
questions.source: Word Building 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Letters are numbered 1=O, 2=P, 3=I, 4=L, 5=E and 6=C. Which number sequence forms POLICE?
questions.explanation: POLICE maps P=2, O=1, L=4, I=3, C=6, E=5, giving 2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 4; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Letters are numbered 1=C, 2=A, 3=D, 4=N and 5=E. Which sequence forms DANCE?
questions.explanation: DANCE uses D=3, A=2, N=4, C=1 and E=5, so the sequence is 3, 2, 4, 1, 5.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 6; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Letters are numbered 1=M, 2=I, 3=G, 4=A and 5=E. Which sequence forms IMAGE?
questions.explanation: IMAGE maps I=2, M=1, A=4, G=3 and E=5. Therefore the sequence is 2, 1, 4, 3, 5.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Append the same letter to LAN, SAN, WOR and SEE to make four meaningful words. Which letter works?
questions.explanation: Appending D gives LAND, SAND, WORD and SEED, all standard English words.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Which suffix can be added to CONSULT, ASSIST, ACCOUNT and CONTEST to form meaningful words?
questions.explanation: ANT forms CONSULTANT, ASSISTANT, ACCOUNTANT and CONTESTANT.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 11; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Add the same letter to the beginning of TOP, COPE, TINK and LOT. Which letter makes meaningful words?
questions.explanation: S forms STOP, SCOPE, STINK and SLOT.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: When YAWN is arranged in alphabetical order, which letter remains in its original position?
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order is A, N, W, Y. W remains in position 3, its original position.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 18; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: From AMPLIFICATION, which word can be formed using its letters?
questions.explanation: MANIA can be made from M, A, N, I and A. ACTOR and MANOR need R; CHAMP needs H, neither of which occurs in AMPLIFICATION.
questions.source: Word Building 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 14; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Letters map as T=5, M=4, H=3, R=2, E=1 and O=0. Which sequence spells MOTHER?
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 5; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Which word is second in dictionary order: THRONE, THRIFT, THROAT or THRILL?
questions.explanation: All words begin THR. THRIFT and THRILL continue with I, which sorts before O in THROAT and THRONE. Between THRIFT and THRILL, F precedes L, so THRILL is second.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Letters H, T, R, U, O and A are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 respectively. Which sequence spells AUTHOR?
questions.explanation: Using H=1, T=2, R=3, U=4, O=5 and A=6, AUTHOR maps A-U-T-H-O-R to 6, 4, 2, 1, 5, 3.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: How many letters in DRAWING remain in the same position after its letters are alphabetized?
questions.explanation: DRAWING sorts to A-D-G-I-N-R-W. Comparing positions 1 through 7 with D-R-A-W-I-N-G, no position contains the same letter.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 14; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: How many letters in DEVELOP remain in the same position after its letters are alphabetized?
questions.explanation: DEVELOP sorts to D-E-E-L-O-P-V. D at position 1 and E at position 2 stay in place; the other positions change.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In SIGNATURE, how many letters lie between the first vowel and the last consonant?
questions.explanation: The first vowel I is at position 2. The last consonant R is at position 8. Positions 3 through 7 contain five letters.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 16; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: How many pairs in PERHAPS have the same number of letters between them in the word and in the alphabet? Count each pair once, in either alphabetic direction.
questions.explanation: Only P-R qualifies: the letters are two positions apart in PERHAPS and two alphabet positions apart (P=16, R=18). The other pairs fail this equality.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 20; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: From EDUCATION, which word cannot be formed using its letters?
questions.explanation: EDUCATE needs two Es, while EDUCATION has one E. ACTION, CAUTION and AUCTION each fit the available letter frequencies.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Which suffix completes all four words: THANK__, CARE__, HOPE__ and USE__?
questions.explanation: FUL gives THANKFUL, CAREFUL, HOPEFUL and USEFUL, all common words. The other suffixes do not form a valid word with every stem.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: How many letters in FLAGSTONE remain in the same position after alphabetical arrangement?
questions.explanation: FLAGSTONE sorts to A-E-F-G-L-N-O-S-T. G remains at position 4 and O at position 7, so two positions are unchanged.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 17; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: How many qualifying letter pairs are in FANCIER? Count each pair once, including either alphabetic direction.
questions.explanation: Five pairs qualify: F-C, A-C, A-E, N-R and C-E. In each, the absolute alphabet-position difference equals the distance between the letters' positions in FANCIER.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 21; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: How many qualifying letter pairs are in BEACON? Count each pair once, in either alphabetic direction.
questions.explanation: E-C qualifies because their alphabet positions differ by 2 and they are two places apart in the word. O-N also qualifies at distance 1. Total: 2.
questions.source: Word Building 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 22; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Arrange PREVENT, PREVIEW, PREY and PREACH in dictionary order. Which word is third?
questions.explanation: The complete dictionary order is PREACH, PREVENT, PREVIEW, PREY, so PREVIEW is third.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Arrange TRANSFER, TRANSIT, TRANSLATE and TRANSPORT in dictionary order. Which word is second?
questions.explanation: After TRANS, the next differing letters are F, I, L and P, respectively. Thus TRANSFER, TRANSIT, TRANSLATE, TRANSPORT; TRANSIT is second.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: From MISSISSIPPI, which word cannot be formed using its letters?
questions.explanation: PIPES requires E, absent from MISSISSIPPI. Each other option is within the source frequencies (M=1, I=4, S=4, P=2).
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Letters are numbered 1=T, 2=A, 3=E, 4=C and 5=R. Which sequence forms TRACE?
questions.explanation: TRACE maps T=1, R=5, A=2, C=4 and E=3. The sequence is 1, 5, 2, 4, 3.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: The letters G, A, R, D, E and N are numbered 3, 5, 1, 4, 2 and 6 respectively. Which number sequence spells GARDEN?
questions.explanation: Read the code in G-A-R-D-E-N order: 3, 5, 1, 4, 2, 6.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: How many letters in BALLOON remain in the same position after alphabetical arrangement?
questions.explanation: BALLOON sorts to A-B-L-L-N-O-O. The two Ls remain at positions 3 and 4, and O remains at position 6: three positions match.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: How many pairs in DECEPTION have the same number of letters between them in the word and in the alphabet? Count each pair once in either alphabetic direction.
questions.explanation: The qualifying pairs are D-E and O-N; each pair is adjacent in the word and adjacent in the alphabet. Therefore there are two pairs.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question
